claim: Under a 332-point thread about Meta shipping facial recognition on smart glasses, a person with prosopagnosia states the requirement and the hard constraint in one sentence: he wants to feed an offline database photos of friends so it can recognise them, and 'Accessibility shouldn't require giving up privacy.' The capability just shipped to the public — built on somebody else's cloud, aimed at strangers.
does: Reads the photos already in your own phone album, on the device, and produces one page for before you walk in: the people you are seeing today, each with the face you would actually recognise them by and one non-facial cue — height, glasses, hair, what they always wear, where you last were together.
edge: It only ever recognises people you already know, it never leaves the phone, and it hands you something you can print or set as a lock screen — so the recognition happens in your head, before the room, instead of on a screen in front of the person.
why_use: Your photo album already clusters these faces on-device; it just refuses to tell you who they are or give you anything you can carry. The alternative that shipped this month puts the same job on a cloud and points it at strangers.
gap: Both halves are mature and nobody has pointed them at this person. Phone albums do on-device face clustering but only group a face with itself — no name, no artefact. The glasses version is cloud-based and aimed outward at people who never consented. Nothing exists that recognises only the people you know, only on your own hardware, only before the meeting.
counter: The cruellest objection is the social act itself: what a face-blind person fears most is appearing rude, and pulling out a phone mid-conversation is ruder than getting the name wrong — so live recognition is essentially a dead path, and what survives is the page you read beforehand, which is worth far less. Second death: Meta has now shipped this in the box; once it is on by default, 'local' is a privacy preference, and people who pay for privacy have always been an order of magnitude fewer than people who say they care about it. Third death: other people's faces — even fully on-device, building a searchable face library of your acquaintances is something a share of people (including the ones in the photos) will judge unacceptable, and a disclaimer does not fix that.
differentiator: The wedge is the ten minutes before, not the moment itself: album in, one page out, nothing uploaded, no camera, no strangers, wipe with one tap. And the audience is wider than the diagnosis — anyone starting a new job with forty faces to learn in two weeks needs the same page. Cold start — English: r/Prosopagnosia, and the Hacker News commenter himself, hand-made first; Chinese: 小红书 / 知乎 「脸盲 怎么记住人」 and 「入职第一周 记不住同事」 posts.
value: One page, made from your own photos, that lets you walk into the room already knowing who is who.
risk: Third-party faces are the real exposure and no self-limit fully removes it; recognition accuracy from casual group photos is mediocre, and a confident wrong name is worse than no name. The population who most need it are also the least likely to talk about it, so distribution is hard and word of mouth is quiet.
method: HN Algolia search for wish-there-was phrasing over the last six months → first-hand comment located under the Meta-glasses story (332 points); index dedupe check for 脸盲/认人/人脸 across 593 radar entries (0 hits).
evidence: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=48404225 — first-hand comment from a person with prosopagnosia stating both the want and the constraint

https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=48403588 — parent story, 332 points: facial recognition shipping on consumer smart glasses (the window that just opened, and the wrong-side-of-privacy version of it)

voices.quote: I wish something like this existed that was completely offline. I'm face blind (prosopagnosia) so being able to feed an offline database photos of friends so it can recognise them would be great. Accessibility shouldn't require giving up privacy.
voices.user: Hacker News commenter under the Meta-glasses story (332 points)
voices.zh: 我希望有一个完全离线的这种东西。我是脸盲（面孔失认症），所以能把朋友的照片喂给一个离线的库、让它替我认出人来，那就太好了。无障碍不该以交出隐私为代价。

consumer_angle: A person with face blindness, or anyone in week one of a new job with forty names to learn, walks into the room holding one printed page — built entirely from photos already on their own phone, with nothing uploaded.
hook: Someone who has spent their life failing to recognise colleagues and friends and has no workaround except bluffing. The capability he needs shipped this month — inside a pair of glasses, on a cloud, pointed at strangers — and he said out loud that he will not take it on those terms.

zh.claim: 在一条 332 分、讲 Meta 把人脸识别装进智能眼镜的帖子底下，一位面孔失认症者用一句话同时说出了需求和硬约束：他想把朋友的照片喂给一个离线的库、让它替他认人，而且「无障碍不该以交出隐私为代价」。这个能力这个月刚刚出货——建在别人的云上，对着陌生人开。
zh.does: 在本机读你自己相册里已经有的照片，出一页「进门之前」：今天要见的这几个人，每人一张你真的认得出来的脸，加一条不是脸的线索——身高、眼镜、发型、常穿什么、上次一起在哪。
zh.edge: 它只认你本来就认识的人，只在本机，而且交给你的是一页可以打印、可以设成锁屏的东西——于是「认出来」这件事发生在你脑子里、在进屋之前，而不是发生在对方面前那块屏幕上。
zh.why_use: 你的手机相册本来就在本机把这些脸聚成一堆了，只是它既不告诉你他是谁，也不给你任何能带走的东西。而这个月出货的那个替代品，把同一件事放上了云，还是对着陌生人。
zh.gap: 两半能力都成熟了，却没人朝这个人做。手机相册做本机人脸聚类，但只把同一张脸归到一起——没有名字，没有成品。眼镜那个版本建在云上，朝外对着从未同意过的人。没有任何东西做「只认你认识的人、只在你自己的设备上、只在见面之前」。
zh.counter: 最狠的一条反对来自社交动作本身：脸盲者最怕的就是显得失礼，而聊到一半掏出手机比叫错名字更失礼——所以「现场识别」这条路基本是死的，活下来的只有事前那一页，而那一页的价值小得多。第二个死法：Meta 已经把这功能装在盒子里出货了，一旦默认打开，「本地」就只是一种隐私偏好，而愿意为隐私付钱的人一向比说自己在意隐私的人少一个数量级。第三个死法：别人的脸——即便全程在本机，替熟人建一个可检索的人脸库这件事，会被一部分人（包括照片里的那些人）判为不可接受，而这不是一句免责声明能解决的。
zh.differentiator: 切口是见面前那十分钟，不是见面那一刻：相册进，一页出，不上传、不开摄像头、不碰陌生人，一键清空。而受众比诊断更宽——任何进新公司第一周要在两周内认全四十张脸的人，要的是同一页纸。冷启动第一步：英文＝r/Prosopagnosia，以及 Hacker News 上那位评论者本人，先手工做一份给他；中文＝小红书／知乎「脸盲 怎么记住人」与「入职第一周 记不住同事」这类笔记。
zh.value: 一页纸，材料全是你自己的照片，让你进屋时已经知道谁是谁。
zh.risk: 第三方的脸是真正的暴露面，任何自限都不能完全消除；从随手拍的合照里认人的准确率一般，而自信地给错名字比不给更糟。最需要它的那批人也最不愿意谈这件事，所以分发很难、口碑很安静。
zh.hook: 一个一辈子认不出同事和朋友、除了硬撑没有别的办法的人。他需要的那个能力这个月刚刚出货——装在一副眼镜里、跑在云上、对着陌生人——而他明确说了，按这个条件他不要。
zh.consumer_angle: 一个脸盲的人，或者任何入职第一周要记住四十个名字的人，进屋时手里拿着一页打印好的纸——材料全部来自他自己手机里已有的照片，一张都没上传。

title: The recognition page you read before the room
